title: Upgrade Postgres to fix local time for Vancouver, Edmonton, and Casablanca
summary: Upgrade Postgres to fix local time for Vancouver, Edmonton, and Casablanca
body_markdown:
Some older Supabase Postgres versions ship an outdated` tzdata` package. As a result, local-time conversions such as` AT TIME ZONE 'America/Vancouver'` return incorrect results for three zones that changed their rules in 2026:


- British Columbia, Canada (` America/Vancouver` ): changed on March 8, 2026.
- Morocco (` Africa/Casablanca` ): changed on September 20, 2026.
- Alberta, Canada (` America/Edmonton` ): changes on November 1, 2026.


This issue affects projects that use one of these zones and run a version earlier than 15.19.0.003 (Postgres 15) or 17.11.0.003 (Postgres 17). Versions 15.19.0.003 and 17.11.0.003 include the updated` tzdata` package.


Your stored data and timestamps are not affected. Only the conversion to local time for these zones is wrong.


### How to check and fix your projects#


You can find your version under **Service Version** in[Project Settings > General](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/settings/general) and upgrade from there to get the fix. The upgrade causes downtime, so plan it for a low-traffic window. Some indexes might need a rebuild after the upgrade.


For full instructions, refer to[Wrong local time for Vancouver, Edmonton, and Casablanca time zones](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/wrong-local-time-for-vancouver-edmonton-casablanca-time-zones) .
